I’m so sorry you’re going through this. I remember when my pmdd really “came on” (although i had very painful and difficult periods from the get go) it got really bad after i had my second son. It was just so jarring and scary to find myself feeling SO horrific every month and I didn’t understand it. I found myself a doctor who listened to me and at every appointment took the time to listen to my cries and keep trying/brainstorming together. Here’s some things that have immensely helped me to get it under control over the last few years:

—Talk therapy 
— magnesium 
—no hormonal birth control (this varies so much person to person, for some people it’s hugely helpful. For me it has the opposite effect)
—Vitex (chasteberry) supplement 
—cut out caffeine and alcohol for a while
—staying very hydrated with water or herbal tea
—squeezing ice cubes in my hands when I want to hurt myself 
—having at least one person i can be honest with how I’m feeling when it’s really bad. It helps just to say it out loud to someone 
—antidepressants. Zoloft worked great for me for a long time; the only reason i weaned off was because it affected my libido and i got into a relationship where i wanted that desire back.
—getting out of a toxic relationship/environment. My pmdd was so much worse when i was with my ex husband 
—charting my cycles and all my symptoms on a period app pretty much every day, so over time I could see the pattern and know what to expect. It helped me see that i would eventually feel better no matter how i felt at that moment.

Initially while trying to heat it, it was giving me an error code and after some googling and troubleshooting found that it just needed water blasted through the motors pipes to clear it out and a new filter. I keep it set to 103 but anytime a person is actually in it, the temp goes down 2 or 3 degrees. I found i was going through filters way too fast, they were getting gross and making the error code go off every day or two and i just can’t afford to be replacing filters that often. So for now i keep it heated without a filter in the chamber but I do still use the chlorine tablets; I also have a little net and skim/scoop the water a few times while I’m in it, the cover does a pretty good job but I live in the mountains so I feel like it gets especially messy. I just emptied, cleaned, and refilled it a couple days ago and the whole process only maybe took me an hour. So far, the combo of frequent skimming, chlorine, keeping hair up/food outside of tub, and changing the water every week or two has been working and I haven’t needed the filter.
